extracted.intended_audience: SNSF management, programme managers, research funders, policymakers and stakeholders in research funding
extracted.subtask_description: Synthesis and evaluation of the Ambizione funding scheme against its objectives (e.g. scientific independence, knowledge transfer, reintegration, attractiveness to foreign researchers, gender and mobility suitability) using surveys, interviews, case studies and administrative data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact on career development (professorships and long-term positions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether Ambizione grantees obtain professorships and long-term positions at greater rates than comparison groups (e.g. share of former grantees working as professors; share with long-term perspective).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use survey and administrative data to compare shares across groups (example figures: 58% of Ambizione postdocs worked as professors after funding vs. 48% for SNSF project beneficiaries and 25% for rejected applicants). Note small sample sizes and differing group sizes as a limitation; distinguish SNSF-funded professorships (time-limited) from permanent positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the extent to which Ambizione contributes to grantees’ scientific independence, including discipline-specific meanings (ability to choose research questions, methods, publish as lead author, acquire funding, supervise staff, lead a group, create collaborations, be invited to conferences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine self-reported survey responses, open-ended qualitative definitions by discipline (Table 15 lists frequent aspects), and external assessments (hosts' comparisons). Example: ~90% of grantees reported Ambizione contributed substantially to their independence; 97% of hosts said grantees were more independent than regular postdocs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to knowledge transfer to Switzerland
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether Ambizione facilitates transfer or retention of knowledge into the Swiss science community (e.g. win-back of returnees, retention of incoming grantees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track current employment location of former grantees after funding (Table 17). Use proportions retained in Switzerland as evidence (e.g. all 36 surveyed returnees who finished funding remained working in Switzerland and in science). Consider long-term vs short-term stays when interpreting knowledge transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitating reintegration for returning researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether Ambizione helps Swiss researchers abroad to reintegrate into the Swiss science community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use survey responses from grantees classified as returnees (e.g. 81% of returnees said Ambizione helps reintegrate; 71% said the possibility to return was a significant reason to apply). Consider differences across target groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attracting and integrating researchers from abroad (incoming)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure Ambizione’s suitability and effectiveness in attracting foreign researchers and supporting their integration into the Swiss science community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use survey data of incoming grantees (e.g. ~90% of incoming grantees agreed Ambizione is suitable for foreign researchers to integrate). Also consider host perspectives and retention after funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for researchers with limited mobility
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the funding scheme is appropriate for researchers with limited international mobility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey and interview evidence should be used; results in this evaluation were inconclusive and many respondents thought Ambizione was not particularly suitable for limited mobility (over 45% negative). Recognise small sample sizes for this target group as limiting inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for female scientists / gender equality
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate representation and success of female applicants/grantees and whether Ambizione offers adequate funding to women.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider share of female grantees vs target value (35%), success rates by gender (noted lower success rates for women but remaining above ~20% except 2013), and possible measures (monitoring, temporary quotas, board composition). Note many respondents could not evaluate suitability for women.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reach and targeting of the funding scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether Ambizione reaches its intended target groups (returnees, incoming, limited mobility) and whether it satisfies their specific needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use distribution of grantees across target groups, reasons for not applying (perceived ineligibility), and whether the scheme is widely known. The evaluation found largest share were returnees and increasing popularity among incoming researchers; limited mobility group small.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence and appropriateness of the funding concept
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge whether the Ambizione funding concept is sensible, coherent, and matched to the scheme’s goals (balance between breadth and selectivity, flexibility for case-by-case evaluation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider fund distribution (not overly generous nor overly broad), flexibility to evaluate individual applications across disciplines and target groups, and whether the concept aligns with long-term goals like knowledge transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility of implementation and case-by-case evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether SNSF and National Research Council implement intended flexibility in evaluation and handle diverse target groups and disciplines appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence: evaluation shows aspired case-by-case evaluation is being put into practice. Consider how procedural rules and expert board decisions affect flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding duration adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the funding period (three years at time of report) is sufficient for grantees’ projects and career development and whether extension is warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather host and grantee opinions (both requested extension to four years); SNSF supports idea and discussion of four-year period is ongoing. Consider project needs, personnel hiring, and career timing (family, mobility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and adequacy of scientific personnel funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether grantees can hire necessary scientific personnel and whether grant rules permit this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees demanded ability to hire personnel; evaluation notes SNSF already changed regulations to allow hiring such personnel. Consider effect on project execution and host burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative support quality (SNSF support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how well SNSF provides administrative help and support to grantees (responsiveness, low-threshold help).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation finds support is quick and low-threshold. Also consider host institutional support and any reported individual cases of failed integration with limited SNSF options to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration into host institutes and associated difficulties
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate how well grantees integrate into host institutes (infrastructure, supervision, teaching, institutional engagement) and identify difficulties (e.g. lack of infrastructure or financial resources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use surveys, interviews and case studies. Findings: generally good integration; some failed cases; 13% of hosts reported difficulties due to lack of financial resources; 66% of grantees were involved in teaching during funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits for host institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure benefits hosts derive from employing grantees (expanded scientific profile, additional research funds, improved networks, supervision/teaching contributions, prestige, low support intensity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey of hosts shows high agreement (e.g. 97% said scientific profile expanded; 74% additional research funds; 71% better connected). Also include qualitative interview evidence (financial benefit, prestige, knowledge transfer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of grantees’ projects and collaborations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the scientific quality of funded projects and the quality of collaboration between hosts and grantees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host survey results: almost all hosts rated project quality and collaboration as good (99% and 97% respectively). Use these ratings alongside external expert assessments and case study evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadweight effect / additionality
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate the deadweight effect (share of grantees who would have had the same outcome without Ambizione) to assess additionality of funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation reports a low deadweight effect (~17%). Use survey questions about alternative funding after rejection and other counterfactual evidence; interpret cautiously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection intensity and balance (breadth vs. excellence focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the scheme’s position between broad funding (many small grants) versus narrow, highly selective funding (few larger grants) and implications for attractiveness and success rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experts highlighted potential trade-offs as scheme becomes more known (increased applicants, lower success rates). Consider strategic decisions about whether to prioritise breadth or selectivity and potential impact on target groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and responding to gender and mobility risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the programme monitors female participation and mobility impacts and whether corrective measures (e.g. quotas, board composition change) are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experts discussed options (temporary quotas, giving preference to female applicants in tie cases, increasing women on expert board). Use trend data (female share above 35% most years) and success rate analyses to inform monitoring needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence limitations and validity considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly consider sample sizes, differing group sizes, and other data limitations when interpreting evaluation results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report warns small numbers of cases (especially for some target groups) and differing group sizes limit validity of some findings (e.g. professorship counts, limited mobility conclusions). Always caveat percentages with sample sizes.
